title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Michael Chen
summary: Company-standardized process and playbook for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. Intended for hiring managers, interviewers, and people-ops partners.
content:
Purpose
This document codifies Redwood Inference's people operations practices for hiring, onboarding, performance cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended to reduce variance between teams, shorten time-to-fill, and improve new hire success and retention.

Scope
Applies to all full-time employees, contractors (when used for multi-month engagements), and hiring managers in North America and Europe. For Private deployment engagements with contractual customer clauses, follow customer-specific onboarding addenda (see related_pages).

1) Hiring process overview
Short intro: Hiring at Redwood follows a standardized workflow to ensure role clarity, an efficient candidate experience, and consistent decision-making. Key owners: hiring manager (HM), people-ops (PO), recruiting partner (RP).

High-level steps (ordered):
1. Requisition creation and approval (HM + PO)
2. Sourcing and screening (RP)
3. Interview loop (HM + interview panel)
4. Debrief & scorecard (panel + HM)
5. Hiring committee & compensation approval (PO + Finance as required)
6. Offer, background checks, and onboarding kickoff (PO)

SLA and thresholds:
- Requisition approval SLA: PO review within 3 business days; final approval within 5 business days.
- Initial phone screen scheduled within 5 business days of candidate passing CV screen.
- Target time-to-offer: 28 calendar days from requisition approval for mid-level roles.
- Offer escalation: any total compensation > 20% above the role band requires VP People + Finance sign-off.

Requisition template requirements (table):
| Field | Required? | Notes |
| Role title | Yes | Use canonical title taxonomy (see job-titles registry). |
| Team / Manager | Yes | Provide manager name and 1-line team mission. |
| Role type & level | Yes | Full-time / Contractor; IC / Manager; Seniority level. |
| Must-have skills | Yes | 3-6 bullet must-haves. |
| Nice-to-have | No | 0-4 items. |
| Target compensation band | Yes | Use approved bands in Compensation Playbook. |

Interview loop design guidance:
- Standard loop for IC engineering roles: Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager screen -> 2 technical interviews (system design + code/perf) -> cross-functional partner interview -> final bar-raiser / leadership.
- Use at least one interviewer from outside the immediate team for calibration.
- No single interviewer should have unilateral veto; decisions are consensus-based.

Scorecard & debrief (required):
- Use the company scorecard template (competencies: role fit, technical skills, collaboration, communication, ownership).
- Each interviewer submits a numerical rating (1-5) and short rationale prior to debrief.
- Debrief meeting must be scheduled within 72 hours of last interview.

Hiring committee & approval flow:
- For all senior-level roles (L6+) and manager hires, submit packet to hiring committee (HC) for calibration: packet = scorecards, proposed offer, and reference check summary.
- HC decision window: 3 business days after submission.

Offer & background checks:
- People-ops owns offer creation and sending; HM drafts offer rationale and business justification.
- Background check vendor: SecureVerify (or equivalent). Consent must be obtained before checks run.
- On acceptance, PO triggers onboarding kickoff within 2 business days.

2) Interviewer responsibilities & fairness guidelines
- Prepare: read candidate resume, scorecard, and any assignment results 24+ hours before interview.
- Behavioral questions should be used to probe ownership and collaboration (STAR format).
- Avoid illegal / discriminatory questions. Use inclusive language.
- Provide timely feedback: submit scorecard within 24 hours of interview.

3) Pre-boarding & Day 0 tasks (PO + IT + HM)
Pre-boarding checklist (to be completed prior to Day 1):
- Create user account(s): corporate email, Slack, GitHub org access request started. Owner: IT.
- Equipment order placed and tracking: laptop + power accessories + any hardware (e.g., GPU keys). Owner: IT/Office ops.
- Paperwork: send offer letter, W-4/equivalent, NDAs, expense policy docs. Owner: PO.
- Announce hire internally (team + company channels) no earlier than candidate accepts and background checks clear. Owner: HM/PO.

Day 1 agenda (example):
- 09:00 — Welcome & HQ orientation (PO)
- 10:00 — Team welcome & role overview (HM)
- 11:00 — IT setup & access verification (IT)
- 14:00 — Immediate contributor goals & 30/60/90 intro (HM)
- End of Day 1 — 1:1 with manager scheduled weekly.

First 30/60/90 plan (template bullets):
- 30 days: onboard systems, complete mandatory training, ship first small ticket, meet cross-functional partners.
- 60 days: own a production change, lead a retrospective, build roadmap contributions.
- 90 days: operate independently on core responsibilities, present a deliverable to stakeholders.

New-hire buddy program:
- Assign a buddy for the first 90 days. Buddy responsibilities: help with tooling, calendar rhythms, and cultural norms. Owner: HM.

4) Performance & feedback cycles
Cadence:
- Weekly 1:1s: manager <> report — coaching and immediate blockers.
- Quarterly check-ins: goals review, mid-cycle calibration, development plan updates.
- Annual review: performance ratings, comp review eligibility, promotion consideration.

Feedback expectations:
- Managers provide timely, specific feedback; employees are encouraged to solicit feedback proactively.
- Use the feedback framework: Situation, Behavior, Impact, Suggested change.

Performance rating scale (summary table):
| Rating | Descriptor | Typical actions |
| 5 - Exceptional | Consistently exceeds and creates major impact | Consider for promotion & spot bonus |
| 4 - Exceeds | Frequently exceeds expectations | Eligible for above-band comp adjustments |
| 3 - Meets | Consistently meets expectations | Baseline performance; eligible for standard merit |
| 2 - Needs Improvement | Inconsistent delivery in key areas | Create Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) |
| 1 - Unsatisfactory | Fails to meet expectations | Consider termination after PIP & review |

Calibration & fairness:
- People-ops runs calibration sessions each quarter to review distributions and remove bias.
- Managers must bring evidence (OKRs, saved deliverables, peer feedback) to support ratings.

Performance improvement process:
- Informal coaching first, documented in 1:1 notes.
- If insufficient improvement after 60 days, manager + PO design a PIP with clear objectives, owner, and timeline (usually 60–90 days).
- Escalation: unresolved PIP issues escalate to Head of People and Head of the hiring organization.

5) Manager playbook: core responsibilities
- Hiring & onboarding: build clear role statements, partner with recruiting, and own first 90 days success.
- Team performance: run regular 1:1s, set OKRs, track deliverables, and provide developmental feedback.
- Career development: hold career conversations twice per year, maintain growth plan documentation.
- People safety & conduct: act promptly on conduct concerns; contact People Ops within 24 hours if an incident is reported.

Manager checklist (first 30 days for new managers):
- Complete manager onboarding training (PO).
- Schedule recurring 1:1 cadence with each direct report.
- Review each direct report's current objectives and recent feedback.
- Schedule a skip-level intro with your manager.

6) Templates & artefacts (where to find)
- Job requisition template: /confluence/company-handbook/templates/job-requisition
- Interview scorecard: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/interview-scorecard-template
- 30/60/90 template & learning plan: /confluence/company-handbook/templates/30-60-90-template
- Performance review form & rating guidance: /confluence/company-handbook/templates/performance-review-form

7) Common edge cases & runbooks
- Counter-offers: HM and PO must evaluate business impact; all counter-offers > 15% require executive review.
- Rehires: treat as new hires; complete full background check.
- Contractor conversions: use conversion approval checklist; comp adjustment requires People Ops + Finance sign-off.

8) Ownership, metrics & reporting
Owners:
- People Ops (PO): hiring workflow, offer letters, background checks, company onboarding program.
- Recruiting (RP): candidate sourcing, initial screens.
- Hiring Manager (HM): interview loop design, final hiring decision rationale, onboarding execution.

Key metrics tracked (people-ops dashboard):
- Time-to-fill (median by role family)
- Offer acceptance rate (target > 65%)
- New-hire 90 day retention (target > 90%)
- Hiring diversity metrics (applied / interviewed / hired funnels)

9) Related policies & resources
- Total Rewards & Compensation Playbook (comp bands and equity guidelines).
- Code of Conduct & Harassment policy.
- Security on-boarding for sensitive roles (see security-and-compliance).

10) FAQs
Q: Who signs offers?
A: People Ops issues offers; signatory for compensation >50% above midpoint is the Head of People.

Q: How are interview disputes resolved?
A: Submit dispute to People Ops; we run a calibration review and may request additional interviews.

Q: What if a new hire’s background check flags an issue?
A: PO reviews details with legal; decisions made on a case-by-case basis and documented.
